# Titan axle, differential and brake swaps

> **Some safety-critical values on this page are not confirmed** (marked [Unverified] or [Partial]): they come from one source or are only partly supported. Verify against the factory service manual before use; later runs re-check them against new sources.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Install the Titan front axle assembly and remove the original driveshaft. [t247]

Swap the front axle from a Titan to match an existing rear setup. [t247]

[Partial] Source a 2011 PRO-4X rear axle and swap existing M226 axles to match. [t247]

[Partial] Replace the Xterra's front suspension with a Nissan Titan M205 unit and install two new Titan CV halfshafts. [t462]

[Partial] Install two new upper control arms and two new lower control arms from the Titan. [t462]

Secure the new front differential using twelve M205 halfshaft flange bolts or nuts. [t462]

[Partial] Install eight new 14mm front drive shaft bolts or nuts and fit two new 32mm halfaxle/hub nuts. [t462]

[Partial] Fill the new front differential with three quarts of 80W-90 or 75W-90 synthetic gear oil. [t462]

Install a pair of tie rod extensions to adjust steering geometry. [t462]

[Partial] Fit 1-inch spacers to the suspension if additional lift is desired. [t462]

[Partial] Apply anti-seize grease to all bolt threads, especially cam and suspension bolts. [t462]

[Partial] Replace halfaxle castle ring pins if the new ones did not come with them. [t462]

Lengthen front ABS lines by bypassing connectors and hard-wiring an additional 12 inches of wire to both sides. [t462]

[Partial] Perform a garage alignment using a sharpie and measuring tape to center the steering wheel. [t462]

Replace the spherical bearings on both sides of the lower control arm. [t462]

[Partial] Install extended front brake lines to accommodate the wider spindle position. [t462]

Verify the VDC system recalibrates or turns off after a brief test drive if the steering wheel sensor is confused. [t462]

[Partial] Install a Titan rear differential and mount rough country upper control arms to handle increased articulation. [t265]

[Partial] Install new CV axles to replace extended options. [t265]

[Partial] Install a used or rebuilt Titan front differential, then swap in CV axles from a Nissan Pathfinder. [t797]

Consider buying used parts from individuals or a junkyard. [t266]

## Tips & gotchas

- Use wheel adapters to change the lug pattern if keeping Xterra wheels. [t247]
- Consider using a Fat Bob brake booster if keeping the stock Xterra master cylinder. [t247]
- [Partial] If mixing a Titan front with an Xterra rear, buy another set of 4.08 gears for the Titan end. [t247]
- [Partial] Use on cam bolts and suspension bolts specifically. [t462]
- [Partial] Prevents mangled lower coil over bolts after high mileage. [t462]
- Ensure pins are replaced to avoid mangled hardware from previous removals. [t462]
- [Partial] Check that halfaxles have castle rings and corresponding pins installed. [t462]
- This is often necessary due to the new outboard position of the spindle and added travel. [t462]
- [Partial] Most Titan swaps do not require this unless using a specific setup (e.g., 3-inch BL). [t462]
- Use this method if the VDC/Slip light indicates a turning sensor error after installation. [t462]
- Look for mangled lower coil over bolts as a sign of worn spherical bearing races. [t462]
- [Partial] Replace both sides even if only one is visibly damaged due to the linkage effect. [t462]
- [Partial] Often overlooked but necessary for significant lift or wide stances. [t462]
- The author assumed this was already done, suggesting it is a common oversight. [t462]
- The Slip light may come on and try to brake the 'spinning' front wheels before settling. [t462]
- [Partial] A quick test drive usually resolves the VDC confusion without complex wiring. [t462]
- [Partial] Consider parts brokers in Georgia for reasonably priced differentials. [t265]
- [Partial] Select a differential over extended axles to allow for future upgrades. [t265]
- [Partial] Consider buying from a junkyard as the cheapest option. [t266]
- Look for parts sold by individuals who found them rather than new inventory. [t266]
